brief.angle: Maintaining a 20-turn chat history requires reprocessing the early messages 20 times, making the last reply 20 times more expensive than the first.
brief.measure: Cumulative prompt token processing cost in non-cached sequential chat sessions.
brief.calc: Turn 1 = 100 tokens processed; Turn 20 = 2,000 cumulative context tokens reprocessed; total processed = 21,000 token reads.
brief.why_now: Longer context windows lead users to keep single chat threads open indefinitely.

problems: 9 statements need a web check, but web search is unavailable right now, so nothing can be verified. Use only numbers you derive by arithmetic, or leave the statements out

spec.title: Why long chat history costs 20 times more per turn
spec.summary: Reprocessing context on every turn makes turn twenty take 20 times more token reads than turn one, totaling 21,000 reads across twenty turns.

beats.say: Your twentieth reply costs twenty times more token reads than your first.
beats.cap: Message 20 takes 20x more work than message 1.

beats.say: Each turn sends the full chat history back to the model.
beats.cap: Every turn re-reads the full past history.

beats.say: If each turn adds one hundred tokens, turn one reads one hundred.
Turn two reads two hundred. Turn twenty reads two thousand.
Your first hundred tokens get re-read twenty separate times.
Across twenty turns, total reads reach twenty-one thousand tokens.
Twenty-one thousand tokens equals re-reading eighty pages of homework.
beats.cap: 21,000 tokens equals roughly 80 pages of homework.

beats.say: The phone battery processes old context repeatedly instead of new answers.
Turn twenty takes twenty times the token processing of turn one.
beats.cap: Turn 20 takes 20x the work of Turn 1.

beats.say: Starting a new chat resets the next turn back to one hundred tokens.
beats.cap: A new chat resets turn cost to 100 tokens.
